title: Series Resistance Increase from Solder Degradation
introduction: Series resistance increase is the electrical performance loss that occurs as fatigue cracks grow through PV module solder joints. Even before a crack spans the full joint cross-section and produces an open circuit, progressive crack growth reduces the effective cross-sectional area carrying current, increasing the electrical resistance of the interconnect. This increased series resistance causes power loss proportional to I²Rs with every increment of current flow, reducing fill factor and maximum power output. The series resistance increase is a measurable indicator of progressive solder joint degradation under field thermal cycling.
reasoning: The 1261-MDPI study explicitly identifies increasing series resistance as the electrical performance consequence of solder crack growth, linking it to the I²Rs power loss mechanism that reduces module output.

key_findings.claim: Open circuits and crack growth in solder joints increase the electrical series resistance, causing I²Rs power loss
key_findings.detail: An open circuit in the solder joint increases the electrical resistance across the interconnect. [^mdpi1261a] Power loss from solder degradation is linked to increasing series resistance (Rs) through the relation I²Rs. [^mdpi1261b]
